verdict.rationale: Nitrokey ships an official command-line tool, nitropy, and a Python SDK. A runtime probe confirmed nitropy installs from PyPI and runs non-interactively. A community user also reports running a Nitrokey HSM on a code-signing server, which suggests unattended use. However, there is no documentation of CI pipelines or unattended device operation, and the touch-confirmation feature on the Nitrokey 3 implies a physical presence step that may limit fully headless use. Missing for 10: documented CI/headless workflows, non-interactive PIN and touch handling for automation, and hands-on corroboration beyond a version check.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Nitrokey's official nitropy CLI installs keylessly from PyPI and identifies itself
The official Python SDK also resolves on PyPI (nitrokey 0.4.2).
Used the original Nitrokey HSM model on a code-signing server project.
